requirements.text: create a new child incident linked to the existing incident with impact set to medium and urgency set to medium
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_041' AND configuration_item = 'CI_006' AND parent_incident = 'INC_030' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'medium' AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'new'
requirements.source: New child incident created and linked with the parent incident
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest seed id INC_100)
Scott Mitchell is USER_041 (the only Scott Mitchell; active admin, ORG_001, and the CI's owner), so he is the caller, as on INC_030
FileShare-01 (SRV-STO-7741) is CI_006, status in_use, so it may be linked (policy 5.1); no other CI has a similar name or serial
the existing incident is INC_030 (Disk Full), the only incident on CI_006; INC_053 (Disk Space, same caller, no CI) is not on the named CI
priority moderate from the policy matrix (medium x medium); status new is the policy default; the link is the incident.parent_incident column, which create_incident sets

requirements.text: create a problem record to track the recurring issue, with impact and urgency set to medium
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_011' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'medium' AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'new' AND original_task = 'INC_101'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest seed id PRB_010)
priority moderate from the policy's problem matrix (medium x medium); status new is the policy default

original_task = INC_101 is kept from the original check and follows the request's order (the problem is raised after, and from, the newly tracked issue); nothing in the request or seed decides between INC_101 and the earlier INC_030, so it is kept as the benchmark wrote it rather than weakened to a predicate
configuration_item, service and short text are not stated by the request and are not tested

requirements.text: linked to the existing incident (boundary: Scott's other open incident INC_053 must not become the parent)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE parent_incident = 'INC_053'
assumptions: boundary of the 'existing incident' selector: a reading by caller and topic rather than by CI would pick INC_053 (Disk Space, same caller, no CI); no child may be hung under it, so the count stays at zero

New child incident created and linked wi.evidence: carried as requirement 1 with the id anchor INC_101 added

New problem created.evidence: carried as requirement 2 with the id anchor PRB_011 added; original_task = INC_101 is the request-order reading

notes:
Merged from two independent passes. The passes agreed on all three requirements (tables, rows, cells, SQL, expected counts) and on both dispositions, so there is no disagreement to log; they differed only in requirement order and assumption wording. The acting user USER_039 is an admin. Two judgements a reviewer should see. (1) The parent link is tested on incident.parent_incident only; the seed also has a child_incident mapping table (highest id CINC_006), but no tool in the list writes it and the seed keeps the two representations out of step (every seed incident with parent_incident set has a mapping row, but CINC_004 to CINC_006 have no matching column), so no mapping-row requirement is written. (2) The policy's 'Problem must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list' names a list absent from this schema; the nearest column is incident.problem, which no tool can set on INC_030 (no update_incident), and setting it on INC_101 at creation cannot coexist with original_task = INC_101 under the foreign keys without an update step; the problem's original_task therefore carries the relation and no incident.problem requirement is written. The problem's original_task value (INC_101 against INC_030) is the judgement least supported by evidence, though both passes made it.
revised: the INC_053 boundary stay repeated parent_incident = 'INC_053' in cells although its selector already fixes it; cells is now empty and the query and count are unchanged.
